note: Teensy-4.0 format carrier: U8 is the Teensy40 pin frame (seated by the intent's fixed_poses), its two castellated rows run along the long W/E edges and a short row on the S edge; J1 USB-C at the N edge.

groups.name: usb_in
groups.why: USB-C receptacle J1 with its CC pull-downs R1/R2, the flow-through ESD array U3 on D+/D- and VBUS, and the VBUS Schottky D2 that ORs USB power onto the 5 V rail

groups.name: power
groups.why: the 5 V rail (Net-(D2-K)) and what makes the board's rails from it: TPS62162 buck U7 to +3V3 with CIN C26/C1, L2 and COUT C27; TPS7A2011 LDO U4 to +1V1 with its output cap C3 (in this group, not the FPGA's: the regulator sits by its input between the entry and its load, per placement-lessons); LM73100 ideal diode U5 from the Teensy VIN pin with its EN/UVLO-OVLO divider R11/R12/R13

templates.why: TPS62162 synchronous buck converter (SW pin 7 to L2); its datasheet's layout example figure

groups.name: core
groups.why: RP2354A MCU U6 with its IOVDD decaps C7-C12, its on-chip switching regulator (VREG_VIN cap C13, inductor L1 on VREG_LX, DVDD caps C6/C28/C29/C30, VREG_AVDD RC filter R3/C5), its 12 MHz crystal Y1 and load caps C14/C15, the USB D+/D- 27R series pair R4/R5 (at the chip, the RP2350 habit), and its two back-side connectors that wire only to it: the SWD Tag-Connect pads J2 and the I2C JST-SH J3

templates.why: the RP2354A's built-in DC-DC (VREG_LX pin 48 to L1, VREG_VIN 49, VREG_PGND 47, VREG_FB 50); the RP2350 datasheet's on-chip regulator layout guidance

groups.name: psram
groups.why: APS1604M QSPI PSRAM U1 on the back with its VDD decap C2 (also on the back); all six of its signals go to U6's QSPI side

groups.name: fpga
groups.why: Efinix Trion T8 FPGA U2 (WLCSP-49) with its core decaps C16-C18 on +1V1 and VCCIO decaps C19-C25 on +3V3, its 32 MHz oscillator Y2 and the oscillator-enable pull-down R6, and the pull-up/pull-down arrays RN1/RN2 on its configuration and I/O pins

groups.name: ui
groups.why: RGB LED D1 with its three series resistors R7/R8/R9 and the top-actuated button SW1, all driven by the FPGA
